title: Fuzzy session aliasing and weighted credit allocator for late-arrival & cross-edge token attribution
creator: Arielle Wong
description:
Problem: Incoming token events for a single user session currently arrive from multiple edge proxies and the hosted API gateway with inconsistent session IDs and partial identifiers (device_id, ephemeral_conn_id, proxied_client_id). This causes orphaned token records, double-counting during late-arrival windows, and brittle backfills for chargebacks. Existing reconciliers only operate on exact-session keys or very wide time-window joins which either miss matches or produce high false merges.

Goal: Implement a deterministic, auditable fuzzy-aliasing layer in the ingestion pipeline that emits a canonical session alias with a confidence score and provenance metadata. Use those aliases in a new weighted-credit allocator that splits or merges token consumption across candidate sessions according to confidence + business heuristics (customer-owned session anchors, paid seat mapping, route priority). This should reduce orphaned tokens by >= 95% in the 48h late-arrival window and ensure billing invariants (no net token creation, explainable allocations).

Scope:
- New ingestion step in the streaming pipeline (kafka consumer -> aliasing service -> enrichment -> ledger write).
- Algorithm: deterministic fingerprinting + probabilistic match scoring (token-level key overlaps, IP/ASN affinity, device fingerprinting, route/model affinity, temporal proximity).
- Output: canonical_alias_id, confidence_score (0.0-1.0), provenance (list of matched keys as string), chosen_strategy (merge|split|hold).
- Weighted-credit allocator: consumes alias stream and existing per-tenant charge rules to produce per-tenant/per-invoice token allocations, persisted in the token_escrow ledger table with audit columns.
- Shadow-run & canary: run in shadow for 2 weeks with replay validation and reconciler comparator metrics before swapping write paths.
- Observability: dashboards for alias volume, confidence distribution, pct-orphan reduction, allocator split-rate, and downstream billing divergence.

Constraints & trade-offs:
- We must not introduce non-idempotent writes to the ledger. Allocator must produce idempotent batches keyed by alias and ingestion window.
- For high-confidence merges, prefer merging at ingestion; for low-confidence, create escrow records and route to billing adjudicator for manual review. This reduces incorrect auto-merges at cost of more manual triage.
- Performance SLO: additional latency at ingestion must be < 50ms p95 for steady-state traffic; batching permitted for large bursts but must not degrade downstream realtime dashboards beyond 30s.

Why this is different from prior work: Prior reconciler tickets focused on deterministic, exact-key joins or epochal window compaction. This ticket implements a confidence-driven allocation approach that emits provenance and supports split allocations rather than forcing a single ownership outcome, enabling both better accuracy and explainability for finance and CS teams.
acceptance_criteria: Streaming aliasing service deployed (k8s) with a defined protobuf avro schema and schema registry entry: canonical_alias_v1
Alias stream contains canonical_alias_id, confidence_score, provenance_keys, chosen_strategy for >= 99% of inbound sessions
Weighted-credit allocator produces idempotent ledger writes to token_escrow with allocation_reason and allocator_version tags
Shadow-run comparator metric shows >95% orphan reduction vs baseline and <0.2% net token delta after reconciliation across a 7-day replay dataset
Latency: aliasing adds <50ms p95 to critical ingestion path; allocator batch commits complete within 2s for 1k aliases
Dashboards: alias confidence distribution, orphan-rate, allocation split-rate, and per-tenant divergence created and linked in the ticket
Rollback plan: feature flag exists to switch back to exact-key pipeline with less than 5 minutes of switching time and no ledger inconsistency
comments: 2026-01-19 — Arielle Wong: Kickoff meeting notes uploaded; initial design doc in Drive (drive.redwood.com/docs/aliases-design). Decided on protobuf for streaming schema and Avro registry for historical compatibility.

2026-01-23 — Marco Salazar: POC for fuzzy matching completed. Used locality-sensitive hashing + time-decayed overlap scoring. Early numbers: ~72% match rate at confidence>0.8 on sampled traffic (last 7 days). PR: github.com/redwood/ingest/pull/2487

2026-01-27 — Priya Menon (Finance): Requested explicit allocation_reason + allocator_version columns for auditability. Also requested 'anchor' flag when customer-provided session id is present to bias merges.

2026-01-30 — Marco Salazar: Implemented idempotent write token (allocation_id = sha256(alias_id + window_start + allocator_version)). Running local integration tests against ledger service with no conflicts.

2026-02-01 — SRE: Load test reached 2.5x peak; ingestion latency p95 increased to 65ms. Action: introduce batching window of 100ms for alias scoring and add async fallback to 'hold' strategy under backpressure.

2026-02-03 — Arielle Wong: Updated acceptance criteria to include p95 latency requirement and shadow-run comparator thresholds. Added dashboard ownership (analytics infra team) and rollout plan to release notes.
